Understanding the Federal Reserve Interest Rate Decision. The Federal Reserve Interest Rate Decision is a policy announcement by the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC). It is one of the monetary policy tools the US Federal Reserve uses to control the country's economy. When the FOMC decides to raise interest rates, it signals that it wants to slow down economic growth and keep inflation in check. When the FOMC raises interest rates, it increases the cost of borrowing for companies, resulting in lower profits and a decrease in the stock market. Conversely, lowering interest rates usually results in a decrease in the value of the USD as lower rates make USD-denominated assets less attractive, leading to a decrease in demand for the currency. However, it is important to note that the Federal Reserve Interest Rate Decision is just one of many factors that can impact the financial markets.
